title: Existing-project adoption state (knowledge/_adoption/STATE.yaml)
description: T81 — the one file that tracks a project being adopted into this framework: what the legacy material was checked for before starting (T86), which import stages have run (T82-T85), who approved each one, and who signed off on the validated result (T88). Same shape and same discipline as bootstrap-state.schema.json (T73), and a separate file on purpose: a greenfield project bootstraps and has nothing to adopt, an existing project adopts and has no discovery stages to settle, and folding both into one state would make each demand the other's stages be settled before it could ever be done.

status.description: Derived from `preflight`, `stages` and `validated_by`/`validated_at` — see adoptionModel.ts's computeAdoptionStatus(). A hand-edited file that disagrees with the derivation is rejected by checkAdoptionState(), not silently trusted. Same rule as T73's bootstrap status and T52's plan Status cell: a value nobody re-derives is a value that drifts.

preflight.description: T86 — what the project looked like before adoption touched it. null until the check has been run, which is why `importing` cannot be reached without it.

stages.description: Exactly one record per T82-T85 import stage, in a fixed order (see ALL_ADOPTION_STAGES).

validated_by.description: T88 — the person who checked the migrated result against the legacy material and accepted it. A name, not a role: same reasoning as knowledge-conflict.schema.json's decided_by.

blockers.description: Work the legacy project had in flight when adoption was about to start — an unfinished task, an open QA issue, an unresolved security finding. Adoption does not refuse outright: a person acknowledges them, because only a person can say whether importing on top of half-finished work is safe here.

notes.description: What the check looked at and found nothing wrong with, so an empty `blockers` reads as "checked" rather than "never ran".

knowledge_ids.description: Items this stage produced (T61 ids) — how adoption and the knowledge base cross-check each other, and what T88 validates against the legacy material.

contract_ids.description: T82 — legacy agent names this stage staged a draft contract for. Names, not knowledge ids: an agent is not a knowledge item, it is the other half of a role (see layout.yaml's agent concept), so it gets a staged contract file rather than a `kind`.

conflict_ids.description: Items this stage re-derived with different content, but did not overwrite because a person had already moved them past `draft`. Same meaning, same reserved-word reasoning, as bootstrap-state.schema.json's field of this name.

approved_by.description: T81's per-segment checkpoint. A person's name. Required before adoption can complete — unlike T73's bootstrap, which asks once at the end, this asks after every stage, because a legacy import that got one document's meaning wrong is cheaper to catch before the next three are built on top of it.
